bullets.title: S&P +1.5%, Nasdaq +2.1% on Iran Diplomacy; Oil Falls 5%, Bonds Rally
bullets.body: U.S. equities surged Monday with the S&P 500 up 1.5% (approaching record highs) and NASDAQ +2.1% after Trump signaled Iran talks and called off a planned strike, sending Brent crude down 4.7% to $83.77/bbl and WTI down 5.1% to $80.34. Bond yields declined (10yr -1.9bps to 4.665%) as Middle East risk premium unwound. S&P futures were up an additional 0.3% in Tuesday pre-market.

bullets.title: Trump Drafts Ban on Chinese Data Center Components; Optical Names Rally 9-18%
bullets.body: The Trump administration is drafting a ban on U.S. imports of new Chinese optical transceivers for data centers (FCC also involved), targeting Chinese suppliers like Innolight (~27% global share) and forcing hyperscalers toward domestic suppliers. COHR +17.8%, LITE +13.3%, FN +13.6%, CIEN +10%, GLW +9.5%, MRVL +8% rallied sharply in pre-market. JPM notes the ban would likely cause near-term supply constraints and higher costs for U.S. buyers given domestic suppliers lack scale.

bullets.title: PLTR +15% After-Hours: US Commercial Accelerates to 149% YoY; FY Guide Raised to 82%
bullets.body: Palantir reported Q2 revenue of $1.94B (+93% YoY), beating consensus $1.81B by 7.5%, with US Commercial at $764M (+149% YoY, accelerating from 133%) and US Government +90% YoY. FY26 revenue guidance raised to $8.15-8.16B from $7.65-7.66B (+82% growth). FCF guide raised to $4.7B; non-GAAP operating margins hit 62%. Multiple brokers raised PTs: Citi to $245, UBS to $220, Mizuho to $215, Piper OW $230. CEO set internal 18-month target for total company growth to approach US Commercial levels (>100%).

bullets.title: Macro Regime: 'Normal Expansion' Intact; Yields Would Need 5.75% to Change Regime
bullets.body: Quant macro model continues to classify the environment as Normal Expansion with expectation to persist in 2H26. The 10yr yield must rise to ~5.75% to materially alter the regime, assuming other variables unchanged. Post-FOMC yield increases now reflect stronger risk sentiment rather than tightening fears, which favors Risk-On, Growth, Tech, Deep Cyclicals, and Financials while reducing appeal of Low Volatility and Quality factors. ISM Manufacturing hit 55.6 in July, seventh consecutive month of expansion; US 3Q GDP nowcast spiked to 6.2%.

bullets.title: AI Capex Supercycle: Hyperscalers Confirm Demand > Supply; Cloud Capex Tracker +29% YoY in 2027
bullets.body: Following Q2 results, all four US hyperscalers (META, AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT) expressed greater confidence in CY26-CY27 ROIC supported by rising backlogs and pricing power. AWS CEO says capacity is sold through 2027 into 2028 with demand 'just massive'; Amazon's custom silicon hit a $25B annual run rate. Morgan Stanley's cloud capex tracker now points to 29% YoY growth in 2027 vs. prior 14% forecast. JPM notes management teams demonstrating sufficient ROIC on capex to justify P/E multiple expansion.

bullets.title: DRAM/HBM Sold Out Through 2027; Memory Shortage Creates Pricing Power Across Supply Chain
bullets.body: DigiTimes and multiple broker sources confirm all 2027 DRAM and HBM capacity at SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron is fully booked, with customers receiving only 60-70% of requested volumes. NAND flash expected to fully book by year-end. TrendForce reports AI server shipments +31% YoY in 2026; top 9 CSPs spending $886.7B capex (+90% YoY). NVIDIA is reportedly considering downgrading Rubin Ultra HBM specs due to supply constraints (supply issue, not demand issue per analysis).

bullets.title: ON Semi AI Data Center Revenue to More Than Double in 2026; TAM Raised to $47.5B by 2030
bullets.body: ON Semiconductor reported Q2 revenue $1.60B (beat consensus $1.59B) with EPS $0.74 vs. $0.71 est; guided Q3 to $1.70B with gross margin expanding to 41%. AI data center revenue now expected to more than double in CY26 (tracking to >$500M), with TAM raised to $47.5B by 2030 (72% CAGR from prior $12.2B/40% CAGR). Design wins include NVDA MGX, AWS power supply, and 800V rack architectures. Lead times extended from 27 to 32 weeks; fab utilization rose to 83%.

bullets.title: July Was Record Monthly Drawdown for Asia L/S Funds; Tech/Semi Selloff Driven by Forced Liquidation
bullets.body: GS Prime data shows Asia Fundamental L/S managers down 15.2% in July (largest monthly drawdown on record since 2016), with China L/S down 16.2% and Japanese funds seeing largest dollar de-grossing ever. KOSPI fell 22% in July (worst since Oct 2008) before sharp end-month rally as deleveraging appeared to run its course. SMH saw record $9.4B weekly inflow as semis were aggressively bought; one source notes the July semi selloff was 'caused by forced liquidation, not fundamentals.'

bullets.title: Market Broadening From Mega-Cap Tech Into Industrials, Energy; Goldman Sees Earnings Growth Driving Returns
bullets.body: Goldman AM notes market leadership broadening away from mega-cap tech concentration as AI capex supercycle benefits industrials, infrastructure, energy, and defense. Tech sector has de-rated despite strong earnings as hyperscaler capex erodes FCF yields. Goldman argues earnings growth (not multiple expansion) will drive returns in the higher cost-of-capital environment. UBS equity strategy notes the AI spend cycle is only 2 years in vs. ~10 years for prior tech cycles, with semis/compute trading at 0.8x P/E-to-sales-growth.

bullets.title: July Core CPI Expected at 0.23% MoM; Fed on Hold Unless August Prints Hot
bullets.body: Wolfe forecasts July core CPI at 0.23% MoM (headline 0.16%), driven by reversals in MV insurance and lodging declines. The print would be soft enough to keep the Fed on hold provided August core PCE tracks below 0.25%. Fed economists have shifted their December rate hike forecast from prior 2H27. There is 'little room for error' — firm employment or inflation prints would substantially raise odds of a September hike. Bond market is pricing a full hike by 4Q26 per the forward curve.

bullets.title: Bezos Files to Sell $4.07B in AMZN Stock Under 10b5-1 Plan
bullets.body: Jeff Bezos filed a Form 144 to sell up to 15 million Amazon shares (~$4.07B) under a pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 trading plan. AMZN fell 1.9% after-hours on the filing, though the stock hit a $3 trillion market cap intraday on Monday. AWS remains capacity-constrained with demand described as outstripping supply through 2028.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz Diplomacy: Iran-Oman Deal Progressing; Oil Supply Shock Framing
bullets.body: Aramco CEO warns of 11M bpd supply losses with Hormuz shut (flows currently at 10% of pre-conflict levels) and says it would take 18 months to rebuild global oil stocks post-disruption. An Iran-Oman deal is reportedly being finalized to reopen the Strait, with Iran controlling the entry channel and Oman the exit. Brent settled near $83.77 (-4.7%) on diplomacy hopes; Iran continues to deny direct US talks while acknowledging Oman-mediated shipping discussions.

bullets.title: Biggest Tech Momentum Drawdown Since 2008 Followed by Record Weekly Tech Inflows
bullets.body: BofA reportedly issued a bull/bear signal as the market saw its biggest momentum drawdown since 2008 alongside record-high tech weekly inflows. JPM's Tactical Positioning Monitor fell to ~20th percentile, triggering what they call an attractive setup. Crowded Tech longs were down 21% in North America vs. shorts down 6%; positioning risks remain elevated with Momentum at >90th percentile long-term and Tech Hardware/Semis at 80th percentile.

bullets.title: HBF Memory Standard Advances: SK Hynix, SanDisk, Google, Tenstorrent Launch Open Spec
bullets.body: SK Hynix and SanDisk unveiled the industry's first HBF (High-Bandwidth Flash) standard specifications six months after launching a consortium; Google and Tenstorrent have also joined. HBF is positioned as a hybrid memory layer between HBM and SSDs, offering HBM-like speed with significantly expanded capacity, targeting large model weight and KV cache bottlenecks in AI inference. The standard is seen as complementary to, not replacing, HBM.

bullets.title: Copper Hits Two-Month High at $14,000+/Ton; Iron Ore Falls Below $100 on Deteriorating Fundamentals
bullets.body: Copper rallied past $14,000/ton on the LME to hit a two-month high, while iron ore dropped below $100/ton with UBS warning that 'fundamentals are deteriorating.' The divergence reflects AI/infrastructure-driven copper demand vs. China property/steel weakness. WTI crude oil meanwhile fell 5% to $80.34/bbl on Hormuz diplomacy hopes.

bullets.title: Fed Senior Loan Officer Survey Deteriorates Sharply to -26.8%
bullets.body: The Q2 Fed Senior Loan Officer Survey fell to -26.8% from -12.9% last quarter, signaling significant tightening of bank lending standards. This credit condition deterioration comes alongside the broader risk-on equity rally, creating a notable divergence that warrants monitoring for potential macro regime implications.

bullets.title: Anthropic Secures $10B Computing Deal; Google Backs $200B AI Infrastructure Program
bullets.body: Anthropic entered a $10B computing capacity deal with Volta Infra Holdings for data center access. Separately, Google has assembled a $200B Wall Street finance program backing Anthropic's cloud and TPU capacity. The AI boom is attributed to roughly one-third of recent US economic growth, with AI infrastructure buildout described as the 'largest in human history' by NVDA's Jensen Huang.

bullets.title: AAPL Hit with Multiple Downgrades; India Sales Top $10B for First Time
bullets.body: Apple was downgraded to hold from buy at both China Renaissance Securities (PT cut to $280 from $329, implying 8% downside) and DZ Bank (maintains $310 PT, 2% upside), flagging margin pressures from AI infrastructure costs and supply constraints. Separately, Apple's annual India sales topped $10B for the first time, and the company is facing a MacBook Air shortage due to memory chip supply constraints. Services revenue also missed expectations per Morgan Stanley.

bullets.title: 30-Year Mortgage Rate at 12-Month High; Middle-Income Consumer Outperforming
bullets.body: 30-year mortgage rates hit their highest level in over 12 months, adding to housing market affordability headwinds. However, PSC Macro notes middle-income consumers are benefiting from faster real wage growth and strong labor market conditions, with a middle-income stock basket outperforming consumer staples companies. Gas prices at $4.10/gallon remain a headwind but are down from the May peak of $4.50.

bullets.title: Japan-US Coordinated FX Intervention: $36.6B Yen Buy; USD/JPY Sustainability Questioned
bullets.body: Japan reportedly spent ~$36.6B in coordinated yen-buying intervention with the US on Friday, squeezing JPY shorts and lifting the yen from 40-year lows. However, JPM maintains USD/JPY targets of 160 (3Q26) and 164 (4Q26), arguing that underlying macro factors (negative real rates, fiscal expansion) support resumed JPY selling. BOJ JGB holdings remain significant, keeping downward pressure on term premia.
